title: Grit glossary and mini-probes: customer gripes & quick fixes
body:
Purpose
A compact, jargon-light glossary of recurring customer gripes (the "grit") we keep seeing in field calls plus a set of low-effort exploratory probes we can run in the next 2–4 sprints. This is intentionally operational: quick reproductions, estimated dev effort, one-page experiment plan, and an owner. Use for handoffs to SRE/serving-runtime/product.

Background/context
Over the last 8 weeks CS field notes and NPS followups have converged on ~7 repeat pain points across enterprise and scale-up accounts. Many of these are variants of the same underlying runtime behaviour but expressed differently by customers ("it hangs on long chat history", "embedding results drift", "price jump for short inputs"). We need a small, testable playbook so engineering can prioritise low-risk, high-confidence fixes and we can run quick probes to validate impact.

How to read this doc
- Glossary: short plain-language definition + canonical repro steps.
- Impact tagging: customer-severity (low/med/high), cost-impact (qual/est).
- Probe sketch: goal, hypothesis, steps (2–4), success metric, owner, rough effort.
- Notes and sample quotes: verbatim snippets from CS interviews to help prioritise messaging.

Glossary entries (grit)
1) KV-cache staleness ("context lost mid-chat")
Definition: Long-running chat sessions sometimes receive responses that ignore recently added system or user messages; cache snapshots appear to be serving older KV state.
Canonical repro steps:
- Start a multi-turn chat (1000+ tokens history).
- Insert a system message mid-session, then request a synchronous generation on a new turn.
- Observe mismatch between new system instructions and generated text.
Customer-severity: high
Estimated cost-impact: medium (customer spends more tokens re-asking, increases retries)
Probe sketch:
- Goal: verify whether prefix caching TTL or eviction policy is mis-indexing recent writes.
- Hypothesis: caching layer returns previous KV snapshot when live compaction occurs close to request time.
- Steps: (1) Instrument KV cache to log snapshot versions and request id; (2) run controlled chat sessions that mutate system messages at known timestamps; (3) correlate served snapshot id with final output.
- Success metric: >95% correlation between newest snapshot and response for controlled sessions.
- Owner: Omar Reyes
- Effort: small (2–3 dev days + 1 SRE day)
Notes/quotes: "We changed the bot persona and responses were still using the old style for several turns — we gave up and restarted the session." — enterprise partner

2) Burst latency regression on dedicated pools ("random high spikes")
Definition: Customers on dedicated Reserved pools see sporadic latency spikes (1–5% of requests) that exceed SLO by 3–10x, often coinciding with autoscale events or background maintenance.
Repro steps:
- Use a synthetic workload that mimics production token distribution with intermittent concurrency spikes.
- Monitor per-request trace-level timings around autoscale windows.
Customer-severity: high
Estimated cost-impact: high (missed SLOs can trigger credits / support churn)
Probe sketch:
- Goal: identify whether spikes are caused by cold kernel loads, GC pauses, or network jitter.
- Hypothesis: kernel warm-up after scaling causes initial requests to queue and backpressure into frontends.
- Steps: (1) Add detailed kernel load timing metrics to traces; (2) run scale-up simulation with controlled traffic ramp; (3) compare warm vs steady state latency percentiles.
- Success metric: isolate root-cause in traces for >90% spike events.
- Owner: Daniel Kim
- Effort: medium (1 sprint with infra + runtime)
Notes/quotes: "We saw a 5s tail for ~2% of calls right after an overnight autoscale — kills our SLA."

3) Embedding drift versus baseline ("results less useful over time")
Definition: Similar queries to a model return embeddings that slowly diverge across model updates or quantization changes, hurting similarity searches.
Repro steps:
- Run a fixed corpus of 10k queries weekly against the same model version and any promoted quant variants.
- Measure recall@k for a fixed gold set.
Customer-severity: medium
Estimated cost-impact: medium (app devs add safeguards and reindex more frequently)
Probe sketch:
- Goal: measure drift magnitude when switching quantization profile or kernel variant.
- Hypothesis: 4-bit quant profile with a particular kernel causes small but measurable angular displacement for low-frequency tokens.
- Steps: (1) Create weekly benchmark harness; (2) run AB between float/quant variants; (3) compute embedding cosine drift and retrieval drop.
- Success metric: quantify drift threshold where recall@10 drops >=5%.
- Owner: Mariana Silva
- Effort: small (bench + analysis, ~1 week)
Notes/quotes: "Our search used to return near-perfect names, now top-5 is noisy — suspect model change after April deploy."

4) Tokenization surprises ("billing mismatch")
Definition: Users see unexpected token usage because of pre/post-processing differences across SDKs or because model tokenizer edge-cases break the expected token counts.
Repro steps:
- Submit short and long prompts from SDK A and SDK B (python vs js) and compare per-response token counts in the billing logs.
Customer-severity: medium
Estimated cost-impact: high (billing queries / audit effort)
Probe sketch:
- Goal: reproduce mismatch across SDKs and document tokenizer config differences.
- Hypothesis: default normalization flags differ between SDKs; library update changed behavior.
- Steps: (1) Create minimal repro across SDKs; (2) dump tokenizer outputs and cost logs; (3) propose SDK patch or docs note.
- Success metric: patch or clear doc reduces cross-SDK billing disputes to 0 in next 30 days for pilot customers.
- Owner: Aisha Patel
- Effort: very small (2–3 dev days)
Notes/quotes: "We were billed 3x what we estimated for small prompts — wasted time reconciling with finance."

5) Rollout regressions ("A/B model rollback needed")
Definition: Model rollouts occasionally produce subtle quality regressions for niche prompts; customers want safer canary windows and automatic quick rollback triggers.
Repro steps:
- Run customer-specific eval prompt sets during canary (small sample) and compare to baseline metrics.
Customer-severity: medium-high
Estimated cost-impact: variable (depends on customer sensitivity)
Probe sketch:
- Goal: build faster, per-tenant lightweight evalchecks during canary.
- Hypothesis: a secret set of customer prompts (10–50) can detect regressions early with high precision.
- Steps: (1) instrument canary pipeline to accept per-tenant eval sets; (2) create quick-pass/fail rule; (3) enable automatic fallback if thresholds breached.
- Success metric: time-to-detect regression < 15 minutes and false positive rate < 5%.
- Owner: Product-hosted-api (liaise: Product); CS owner: Daniel Kim
- Effort: medium (1 sprint)
Notes/quotes: "We couldn't surface the regression until it affected prod users — we need per-client canaries."

6) Confusing error surfaces in Private deployments ("500s with no clue")
Definition: Customers running Redwood Private sometimes see opaque 5xx errors with incomplete audit logs, making root-cause analysis slow.
Repro steps:
- Trigger a heavy load and simulate a dependent KMS timeout in a Private deployment; capture logs and audit trails.
Customer-severity: high for Private customers
Estimated cost-impact: medium (support overhead)
Probe sketch:
- Goal: enrich error payloads and correlate local audit logs with the control plane for Private.
- Hypothesis: logging level differences and redaction make useful traces unavailable.
- Steps: (1) add structured error codes with grep-friendly fields; (2) run a simulated failure; (3) verify missing context is surfaced while preserving PII rules.
- Success metric: time to triage drops by 40% in pilot.
- Owner: Private deployments eng + Security liaison
- Effort: small-to-medium (2 weeks)
Notes/quotes: "We had to escalate for a basic 500 and the logs were just 'internal error' — customer unhappy."

Prioritization lens and quick scorecard
- Quick scoring (impact x effort): rank by (customer-severity * estimated business exposure) / effort. Immediate probes: KV-cache staleness, tokenization surprise, error-surface clarity.
- Quick wins: tokenization (very small effort, high customer angst), KV-cache instrumentation (small effort, high severity).
- Investment bets: rollout canaries and autoscale warm-up fixes (higher effort, material SLAs).

Experiment runbook (templated)
- Title: [one-line] e.g., "KV-cache snapshot correlation probe"
- Owner: name + slack handle
- Hypothesis: declarative
- Inputs: customer sample, synthetic harness (link), config toggles
- Steps: numbered small runnable steps
- Data to collect: trace ids, snapshot ids, tokens consumed, sample responses
- Success criteria: quantitative thresholds + subjective customer sign-off for pilot accounts

Communication play (CS + Product)
- For small probes: flag to named CS AE for affected customers, offer pilot window (2 weeks) and clear rollback path.
- For medium/high impact items: schedule customer-facing postmortem template and note potential credits/SLAs.
- Messaging snippets: include one-paragraph plain language explanation and, when appropriate, an optional developer note for technical contacts.

Open questions / unknowns
- Which dedicated customers will allow kernel-level tracing for autoscale probes? Need legal sign-off for host-level telemetry in dedicated pools.
- Are there any model catalog changes scheduled in next 6 weeks that could confound embedding drift probes? Ask model onboarding.
- SDK owners: confirm which versions changed normalization default for tokenizers in March 2026.

Next steps (concrete)
- Week 0: Triage meeting with runtime, infra, and CS (owners assigned: Omar, Daniel, Mariana) — target 2026-05-21.
- Week 1: Run tokenization repro across SDKs, publish short doc with patch or note (owner: Aisha) — target 2026-05-28.
- Week 2: Start KV-cache instrumentation spike (owner: Omar) — target initial logs by 2026-06-04.
- Week 3: Autoscale workload simulation and trace collection (owner: Daniel) — target 2026-06-11.

Appendix: quick evidence snippets
- Transcript excerpt: "We changed system prompt at turn 12 and the model kept responding like turn 3 — lost context, had to refresh." — Customer A (SaaS)
- Billing snippet: sample billing id RED-2026-009 — shows python client tokens 42 vs js client tokens 127 for same prompt (attached repro).
- Linear tickets referenced: RED-3421 (kv suspicion), RED-3499 (tokenizer mismatch), RED-3510 (private error codes)

Use this doc as a live playbook. Move items into sprint backlogs as probes complete and annotate results inline. If a probe confirms a root-cause with a low-effort fix, we should push a release note and an opt-in toggle for affected customers before a full rollout.
